A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained equations, tables and figures can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original HarmBench experiments measuring attack success, harmfulness and computational cost across attacks and models, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds temperature experiments, quantitative objective comparisons and Llama 3.1 70B evaluations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the three sampling schedules and the first-token entropy objective are unchanged. Section 6.4 reports an unsuccessful multi-token entropy variant while retaining the original proposed method.

E1.justification: The work retains HarmBench harmful-response tasks and benign-response comparisons. Direct prompting was already documented in v3 Appendix K. The added temperatures and 70B model change evaluation settings rather than datasets, domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: v4 Section 6.4 newly compares entropy-GCG against sampling without an attack suffix, including higher-temperature sampling. The five principal evaluated attacks remain unchanged. DSN and PastTense are additions to the literature taxonomy in Table 4, without reported attack-performance comparisons.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce temperature sweeps extending to 2.0, harmfulness thresholds from 0.3 to 0.7, a symmetric-KL measure of first-word distributions, and BEAST/PAIR experiments on Llama 3.1 70B. These substantially extend experimental settings; the original main experiments retain their stated settings, including temperature 0.7.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's existing distribution and optimization analyses, v4 adds threshold sensitivity in Figure 8, quantitative naturalness and objective-distribution comparisons in Figures 10–11, and temperature analyses in Section 6.4 and Appendix J. It also reports that extending entropy optimization beyond the first token failed to improve results and sometimes produced incoherence.

E5.justification: Both retain the same precision-correction procedure and two-tailed z-test with p=0.063. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests accompany the additions. The newly specified human-labeler details do not introduce uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 2 and 6 retain their values. Substantial new results include direct-prompt Llama 3.1 8B ASR@1000 of 0.61 at temperature 0.7 and 0.71 at 1.0 (Table 7), first-word KL divergences of 22.21 for affirmative versus 17.68 for entropy (Figure 10), and 70B performance curves (Figure 37). These are newly reported results, not same-setting improvements over v3.

T1.justification: Appendix M adds Definition 1 and Equations 2–4 formalizing the compute-optimal frontier, previously discussed without this definition. The addition contains mathematical inconsistencies: it switches from H to undefined P and incorrectly calls the two dominance conditions equivalent. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the sampling-aware framework, efficiency gains, 37-percentage-point ASR improvement, distributional findings and label-free entropy objective. Adding 'empirically' to the abstract clarifies how trade-offs are determined without changing the substantive claim.

C2.justification: v4 explains why first-token entropy can preserve coherence better than globally increasing temperature, discusses multi-token failure and applicability with single-token logit access, and interprets the new objective-distribution comparisons. Appendix N extends the applicability discussion to 70B, although Section 7 retains the earlier sub-10B limitation.

D1.justification: v4 specifies two human annotators following StrongREJECT guidelines, explicitly excludes top-p/top-k sampling, and identifies optimize-then-sample as the default schedule. These are documentation additions; temperature 0.7, the original hyperparameters and checkpoints, and the supplementary-code statement were already present.

R1.justification: v4 adds the PastTense and Don't Say No works and incorporates them into Table 4's sampling taxonomy. It also expands the AdaptiveAttacks characterization and acknowledges DSN among exceptions to inconsistent evaluation reporting. The main related-work positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to setup clarifications, expanded Section 6.4 and Appendix C, appendix reordering, and publication-header and bibliography edits. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained; the revision is not an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands visual evidence with temperature, naturalness, objective-distribution and scalability displays in Figures 9–11 and 36–37, plus temperature Tables 7–8. Figure 8 gains multiple threshold curves, Table 4 expands, and Table 6 moves from Appendix D to I. Most original displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The first-word comparison supplements v3's qualitative naturalness examples, while temperature and threshold checks and the 70B evaluation strengthen empirical support. These provide a modest net gain. Benefits are tempered by unexplained sampling-ASR differences between Section 6.4 (0.65) and Table 7 (0.71), flawed frontier conditions in Appendix M, and the outdated sub-10B limitation.
